# Summary of the Conservative Party Manifesto 2024

## Economic Vision and Achievements

The Conservative Party's 2024 manifesto, presented by Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, emphasises economic stability following COVID-19 and the Ukraine crisis. The party claims credit for reducing inflation from 11.1% to 2.3%, growing the economy, and creating four million jobs since 2010. Their central message is that abandoning their economic plan would return the UK to instability under Labour.

## Key Tax Pledges

The Conservatives promise significant tax cuts for workers, including halving National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, saving average workers £1,350 annually. Self-employed individuals would see their main National Insurance rate abolished entirely. For pensioners, the "Triple Lock Plus" would guarantee both State Pension and tax-free allowance increases, preventing pension income from being taxed for the first time.

## Immigration and Border Security

The manifesto commits to introducing a legally binding migration cap that falls annually, with Parliament voting on levels each year. On illegal immigration, the party promises regular deportation flights to Rwanda starting July 2024, reformed asylum rules, and continued crackdowns on people smugglers. They pledge to stop small boat crossings by removing the incentive to come to Britain illegally.

## Defence and Foreign Policy

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030—the largest boost since the Cold War. The party commits to unwavering support for Ukraine, modernising nuclear deterrents, and strengthening NATO relationships. They promise a tougher stance on China while engaging where interests align.

## Housing and Planning

The Conservatives pledge 1.6 million new homes through brownfield development, planning reforms, and abolishing EU nutrient neutrality rules. First-time buyers would benefit from permanent Stamp Duty relief up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme. The party commits to protecting the Green Belt while accelerating urban regeneration.

## Public Services

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with plans for 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors. Mental health receives attention through expanded school support teams and community hubs. The manifesto includes 8,000 additional police officers and continued prison expansion.

## Net Zero and Energy

While maintaining the 2050 net zero commitment, the Conservatives take a "pragmatic" approach, promising no new green levies, continued North Sea oil and gas licensing, and investment in renewables and nuclear power, including small modular reactors.

## Young People

A mandatory National Service programme would give 18-year-olds the choice between military or civic service. Education reforms include the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education, mobile phone bans in schools, and 100,000 new apprenticeships.
